name: Bela
overview: Bela was a male descendant of the tribe of Benjamin, specifically identified as the son of Benjamin. He is mentioned among the sons of Israel who went to Egypt, marking him as part of the early patriarchal lineage that entered Egypt during the time of Joseph. His inclusion in the genealogical records highlights his role within the Benjaminite tribe.
namesAndTitles: The name Bela means 'swallower' or 'devourer' in Hebrew, reflecting a proper name given to him that was not divinely assigned. This name appears in the biblical record without additional titles or meanings beyond its literal sense.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Bela as the son of Benjamin. Other familial connections such as relationships to Ard, Naaman, Ezbon, Uzzi, Uzziel, Jerimoth, Iri, Abihud, Abishua, Ahoah, and Gera are inferred from genealogical listings but are not directly stated as his immediate family. Therefore, his primary recorded family relationship is to his father, Benjamin.
scriptureSignificance: Bela's significance lies in his place within the genealogy of Israel as a son of Benjamin, one of the twelve tribes. His presence in the list of those who journeyed to Egypt situates him in the foundational narrative of Israel's sojourn and eventual deliverance. Additionally, the reference to the Belaites in later census records indicates that his descendants formed a recognized clan within the tribe of Benjamin, contributing to the tribal identity and heritage preserved in the biblical text.
